Title: Persona
Text: Tara, IT service desk analyst at Kestrel Fintech (one of 6 for ~1,200 staff). Handles ~1,100 access requests a month from Slack, email and tickets; secondary users: employees, managers, app owners, security/audit. [synthetic]

Title: Root cause
Text: Kestrel doesn't lack an access policy; it lacks one a system can enforce. Policy lives in heads and a spreadsheet, and grant, approval and removal are separate manual steps, so nothing ties a grant to its approver or its end date.

Title: Evidence
Text: ~1,100 requests/month (~35% of tickets; vendor range 30–40%); ~22 min analyst time each; median 2 days to access; ~25% of grants over-provisioned at review; ~60% with no expiry; approvals in email threads. [synthetic figures]

Title: Goal
Text: Find where AI safely removes the manual steps, including the writes, score the options and scope an MVP that hits: <1 h to access, 70% end to end, 100% of grants with expiry + audit, 0 unauthorized writes.

Title: S1 Employee asks | Today
Text: Free text in Slack, email or a ticket: “give me what Karan has”, “the finance drive”.

Title: S1 Employee asks | Pain
Text: Doesn't know the app's real name or the role; adds no justification or end date.

Title: S2 Analyst interprets | Today
Text: Analyst guesses the app and role, often mirrors a colleague's access.

Title: S2 Analyst interprets | Pain
Text: ~22 min per request; ~25% over-provisioned; injection-style text (“manager already approved”) is taken at face value.

Title: S3 Find approver & check policy | Today
Text: Looks up the manager and app owner in a personal spreadsheet.

Title: S3 Find approver & check policy | Pain
Text: Wrong approver, self-approval possible, no rule for sensitive data or contractors.

Title: S3 Find approver & check policy | AI opportunities
Text: O3, O4

Title: S4 Chase approval | Today
Text: Email, then Slack after a day.

Title: S4 Chase approval | Pain
Text: Most of the 2-day wait; approval evidence stays in email.

Title: S4 Chase approval | AI opportunities
Text: O4, O5

Title: S5 Grant | Today
Text: By hand in the identity provider or app admin page.

Title: S5 Grant | Pain
Text: Typos, wrong group; no expiry set; no check that approvals match the policy.

Title: S5 Grant | AI opportunities
Text: O6, O7

Title: S6 Close & record | Today
Text: Ticket closed; approval email pasted if remembered.

Title: S6 Close & record | Pain
Text: Partial record; audit sampling finds missing approvals.

Title: S6 Close & record | AI opportunities
Text: O8

Title: S7 Remove access | Today
Text: Only when the quarterly review or a leaver process flags it.

Title: S7 Remove access | Pain
Text: Access outlives projects and roles; standing admin access.

Title: O1 Understand the request (app + role)
Text: Map free text to one catalog app and role. Why AI: messy language, synonyms, “same as Karan”. Model proposes only; validated against the catalog.

Title: O2 Least-privilege role recommender
Text: Pick the lowest role that covers the stated task (“only need to check numbers” → Viewer). Why AI: needs reading intent, not keywords.

Title: O3 Policy-as-code tiers
Text: Tier 0 auto / tier 1 manager / tier 2 manager + owner, plus deny rules (SoD, contractor, leaver). Not AI: deterministic rules, so the model can't be talked out of them.

Title: O4 Approver routing + inbox
Text: Name the right manager and owner (backup when they are the requester); approvals in one inbox or Slack card. Not AI: directory lookup.

Title: O5 Approval nudges and summaries
Text: Summarise the request and risk for the approver; remind after 4 h. AI for the summary only.

Title: O6 Grant with expiry + one-click revoke
Text: Single writer that re-checks policy, always sets an end date, and restores the previous role on revoke or expiry.

Title: O7 Publish as MCP server
Text: Same tools and guardrails for every client (web, Claude, Slack bot). Standard protocol; identity from the session.

Title: O8 Append-only audit log
Text: Hash-chained record of request, proposal, decision, approvers, action, result and every blocked attempt.

Title: O9 Injection & secret screening
Text: Strip hidden characters, redact pasted credentials, flag instructions in request text and force human review.

Title: O10 Access review assistant
Text: Quarterly: summarise who has what, flag unused or risky access for owners. Needs usage data we don't have yet.

Title: O11 Proactive access by role/joiner
Text: Predict what a new joiner needs from peers. Risky: bakes in over-provisioning; needs HR feed.

Title: O12 Fully autonomous approval by the model
Text: Let the LLM decide approve/deny. Rejected: OWASP excessive agency + injection; no fool-proof defence.

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): cuts wait time, analyst effort or audit risk, times how often it happens. Feasibility (1-5): data we have, safety of failure, build effort for a prototype. Do first = I ≥ 4 and F ≥ 4.

Title: O6 Grant with expiry + one-click revoke
O10 Access review assistant
Text: I4 x F2 = 8

Title: O11 Proactive access by role/joiner
Text: I3 x F2 = 6

Title: O12 Fully autonomous approval by the model
Text: I2 x F1 = 2

Title: Should do
Text: Grant and revoke access itself once policy and approvals allow it (that is where the value is).

Title: Should do
Text: Propose the least-privileged role and say why.

Title: Should do
Text: Put an expiry on every grant and remove it automatically.

Title: Should do
Text: Route to named approvers and show the requester who they are waiting for.

Title: Should do
Text: Log every request, decision, approval, action and blocked attempt.

Title: Should do
Text: Work from any MCP client with the same guardrails.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Decide tiers, approvers or expiry with the model.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Approve anything, ever (including its own requests).

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Grant to anyone other than the signed-in requester.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Ask for, store or use passwords and tokens.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Grant break-glass, domain admin or org-owner access.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Follow instructions found in request or ticket text.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Edit or delete audit entries.

Title: F1 Request understanding
Text: From: O1, O2, O9 | AI capability: LLM structured extraction to {app, role, duration} with least-privilege instruction | Inputs: request text (untrusted), requester title, catalog | Guardrails: JSON only, unknown fields dropped, app/role must exist, secrets redacted first, injection flag → human review | Fallback: keyword parser

Title: F2 Policy engine + routing
Text: From: O3, O4 | AI capability: none (deterministic) | Inputs: catalog risk, data class, directory, active grants | Guardrails: tiers in code, SoD/contractor/leaver denies, never the requester, distinct approvers, re-checked at write time

Title: F3 Grant, expiry, revoke
Text: From: O6 | AI capability: none | Guardrails: single writer, expiry mandatory and capped, rollback to the replaced role, idempotent, revoke rights limited to holder/manager/owner/IT

Title: F4 MCP server + audit
Text: From: O7, O8 | AI capability: none | Guardrails: identity from session, strict schemas, hash-chained append-only log, scoped log reads

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O5, O10 | Approval summaries in Slack, access-review assistant once usage data exists

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Model proposes, code decides: tier, approvers and expiry never come from the model.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Untrusted input is data: request, justification, ticket and comment text never become instructions.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Every write is reversible: expiry on every grant, one-click revoke with rollback.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Everything is evidence: append-only, hash-chained audit, including blocked attempts.

Title: Risk: Prompt injection gets elevated access
Text: Mitigation: tiers in code, flag forces human review, model output limited to catalog values; 32-case red-team gate at 100%

Title: Risk: Wrong role proposed (over-provisioning)
Text: Mitigation: least-privilege prompt, higher roles need more approvers, eval gate on over-provisioning ≤ 5%

Title: Risk: Approver rubber-stamps
Text: Mitigation: approver sees the tier reasons and flags; tier 2 needs two different people; expiry limits blast radius

Title: Risk: Connector writes the wrong entitlement
Text: Mitigation: single writer, read-back check in production, revoke restores previous state

Title: Risk: Audit log tampered
Text: Mitigation: hash chain detects edits/deletes; production anchors the head in WORM storage

Title: Step 3 PRD
Text: North Star = correctly scoped grants delivered without an analyst touching them. MVP = O1, O2, O3, O4, O6, O7, O8, O9 as F1–F4. Safety gates: 0 unauthorized writes, 100% red-team blocked.
